raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### Overview

Three GLM-family MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) models — `glm4_moe_mtp.py` (GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.5-Air / GLM-4.6), `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` (GLM-4.7-Flash), and `glm_ocr_mtp.py` (GLM-OCR) — return the **pre-final-norm** hidden from the MTP layer, so the speculator recycles a hidden that is one RMSNorm short into the next draft step's `hnorm`. The established GLM/DeepSeek-NextN contract (already merged in vLLM by #47448 and also SGLang's `glm4_moe_nextn`/`deepseek_nextn` `vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`) recycles the **post-final-norm** hidden. This PR extends that contract to the three models it missed, and registers them in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` so Model Runner V1 unpacks the new tuple return. Draft-only change; verified output is unaffected.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

Thanks @larryli2-amd. Actually this helped find a real gap, not just missing test coverage. Adding the proposer test revealed the fix was **incomplete**: `SpecDecodeBaseProposer` only unpacks the `(logits_hidden, feedback_hidden)` tuple when `model_returns_tuple()` recognizes the draft architecture, and the three GLM MTP architectures weren't in that allowlist. So on this proposer path, after my change makes the models return a tuple, the proposer would treat it as a single tensor and index it → runtime error. (My earlier GPU runs didn't hit this because they went through the worker speculator path, which unpacks via `isinstance`.)

Fixed in `6ecfab6` by adding `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel`, `GlmOcrMTPModel` to the `model_returns_tuple()` allowlist, alongside the existing `DeepSeekMTPModel` / `Glm5NextMTPModel` / etc.

Tests added:
- `test_model_returns_tuple_recognizes_glm_moe_mtp` — asserts the three GLM architectures report a tuple return (fails without the allowlist entry).
- `test_mtp_propose` — extended to `num_speculative_tokens ∈ {1, 2}` × `{single-tensor, tuple}` returns, so it drives the proposer's actual unpacking path at every draft step for both k=1 and k=2.

One note on the proposer test: `test_mtp_propose` previously only ran at k=1; the k>1 path needs a real attention-metadata type and an initialized `block_size`, which the mocked-model harness doesn't provide. Since this test targets the proposer's tuple handling (not attention-backend compatibility), I disable the `allowed_attn_types` check and set `block_size` in the test, with comments.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

Could we double-check whether the v1 proposer also needs an update for this new tuple-return contract?

`SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` recognizes `DeepSeekMTPModel`, `DeepseekV32MTPModel`, `Glm5NextMTPModel`, and `KimiK3MTPModel`, but not `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel`, or `GlmOcrMTPModel`.

Since the speculative config rewrites these GLM models to the corresponding `*MTPModel` architecture names, it seems possible that the proposer may still treat `(hidden_states, hidden_states)` as a single Tensor. If so, the later indexing or sampling of `last_hidden_states` could receive a tuple instead of a Tensor.

I may be missing another dispatch path here, but would it make sense to update the tuple-return handling for all three architectures, including the corresponding paths in `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` and `glm_ocr_mtp.py`, or otherwise verify this contract in the proposer?

Thanks @larryli2-amd. Actually this helped find a real gap, not just missing test coverage. Adding the proposer test revealed the fix was **incomplete**: `SpecDecodeBaseProposer` only unpacks the `(logits_hidden, feedback_hidden)` tuple when `model_returns_tuple()` recognizes the draft architecture, and the three GLM MTP architectures weren't in that allowlist. So on this proposer path, after my change makes the models return a tuple, the proposer would treat it as a single tensor and index it → runtime error. (My earlier GPU runs didn't hit this because they went through the worker speculator path, which unpacks via `isinstance`.)

Fixed in `6ecfab6` by adding `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel`, `GlmOcrMTPModel` to the `model_returns_tuple()` allowlist, alongside the existing `DeepSeekMTPModel` / `Glm5NextMTPModel` / etc.

Tests added:
- `test_model_returns_tuple_recognizes_glm_moe_mtp` — asserts the three GLM architectures report a tuple return (fails without the allowlist entry).
- `test_mtp_propose` — extended to `num_speculative_tokens ∈ {1, 2}` × `{single-tensor, tuple}` returns, so it drives the proposer's actual unpacking path at every draft step for both k=1 and k=2.

One note on the proposer test: `test_mtp_propose` previously only ran at k=1; the k>1 path needs a real attention-metadata type and an initialized `block_size`, which the mocked-model harness doesn't provide. Since this test targets the proposer's tuple handling (not attention-backend compatibility), I disable the `allowed_attn_types` check and set `block_size` in the test, with comments.

+def test_glm_mtp_layer_recycles_post_final_norm_hidden(
+    default_vllm_config, module_path, class_name
+):
+    # GLM MTP is a DeepSeek-NextN clone. The layer forward must apply the final
+    # norm exactly once (shared_head.norm, fused add+norm over the mtp_block
+    # output + residual) and return that POST-final-norm hidden for BOTH tuple
+    # positions, so the speculator recycles post-norm into the next step's hnorm
+    # and compute_logits consumes it directly. This is the contract fixed in
+    # #47448 and vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py. Returning the single
+    # pre-norm tensor recycled a hidden one RMSNorm short on chained draft steps
+    # (k>=2) — lossless, but lowers draft acceptance.
+    #
+    # A real RMSNorm with NON-UNIFORM weights is used so that a missing, extra,
+    # or wrong normalization is actually caught (a scalar stub would not).
+    import importlib
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
+
+    cls = getattr(importlib.import_module(module_path), class_name)
+
+    hidden_size = 8
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    final_norm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=1e-6)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        final_norm.weight.copy_(torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, hidden_size))
+
+    # Deterministic, distinct block output and residual.
+    block_hidden = torch.randn(3, hidden_size)
+    block_residual = torch.randn(3, hidden_size)
+
+    # Independently compute the expected post-final-norm hidden BEFORE calling
+    # the layer (the fused norm may mutate its inputs in place).
+    expected_post, _ = final_norm.forward_native(
+        block_hidden.clone(), residual=block_residual.clone()
+    )
+    pre_norm = block_hidden.clone() + block_residual.clone()
+
+    layer = object.__new__(cls)

+1 to @larryli2-amd's question on the V1 path — I traced it on main @ 550c1cbb and it does need the registration.

MRV2 unpacks tuple outputs generically (`v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/target_dependent_ar/speculator.py`, `multi_module_mtp/speculator.py`), but `SpecDecodeBaseProposer` only unpacks when `model_returns_tuple()` is true (`llm_base_proposer.py` L600 / L754). Without the new architectures in that set, under Model Runner V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, or any config MRV2 falls back from) `last_hidden_states` is the `(post, post)` tuple and `last_hidden_states[token_indices_to_sample]` (L614) raises — even with `num_speculative_tokens=1`.

A small fix: add `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` to the set in `model_returns_tuple()` and extend the parametrization of `test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py` (that file is in the CPU spec-decode CI job), which also gives the proposer-level coverage asked for above.

Heads-up for reviewers (@larryli2-amd): I've rewritten the tests in this PR in `4275d44` (a normal push on top of the approved head; no force push), following the test-style feedback @fxmarty-amd gave on #62111 (item 5 in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62111#pullrequestreview-5614097052) and `tests/AGENTS.md`, even though nobody asked for it here:

- The `object.__new__` / stub layer test is replaced by `test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, which loads each GLM drafter (GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-OCR configs) through `get_model` with dummy weights and runs its real forward. It fails on the base commit for all three models and passes with the fix.
- The monkeypatched `test_mtp_propose` variants are reverted to their upstream form. Instead, `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/` runs GLM-OCR through `LLM` with two draft tokens on Model Runner V1 and V2. Without the `model_returns_tuple` registration the V1 case crashes (`TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index`); with it both pass. That directory now runs in the DeepSeek + MiMo MTP CI step.

No change to the model or proposer code. Commands and before/after output are in the updated description.
